ns2:section.sectionText: Topics in Art History (Art at its Limits: The 1960s in Brazil, Argentina and the US) An investigation of experimental art in Brazil, Argentina and the United States in the 1960s. Discussion of works that sought to expand and even dissolve the category of "art" through spectator participation, bodily engagement, media interventions, and political activism. Students develop comparative cultural analyses of art-making practices. Attention given to primary texts and visual documentation. Readings include: Umberto Eco, The Open Work; Maurice Merleau-Ponty, The Phenomenology of Perception; Ines Katzenstein, Listen Here Now! Argentine Art of the 1960s: Writings of the Avant-Garde; Roland Barthes, Mythologies; Alexander Alberro and Blake Stimson, Conceptual Art: A Critical Anthology; Marshall McLuhan, Understanding Media: The Extensions of Man. Undergraduate section.
